title: A Echo for the Gravity
premise: Vesper Ravensworth, a cargo navigator who has spent twelve years avoiding the contested shipping lanes of the Kestrel Verge, receives a distress signal broadcast in Old Meridian—a language extinct since the Collapse. Tracing it to a derelict freighter, Vesper discovers two hundred cryosleeping backups: copies of themselves made before the accident that killed their original family, memories intact and waiting to wake. A salvage syndicate wants the hold's contents destroyed because one sleeper carries proof that Earth's final transmission loop—the last message from the homeworld—was falsified by the fleet's founding council. As syndicate hunters close in and the loop's signal decays toward permanent silence, Vesper must choose which half of humanity wakes: the sleepers who remember the truth, or the living crew who need the lie to keep their fragile alliance intact. In the end, Vesper wakes only the sleeper carrying the evidence, broadcasts the true transmission in Old Meridian, and accepts exile—alive, unhidden, and finally singular.
about_author: Casper Yarrow is the pen name of a former merchant-marine radio officer who spent nine years on deep-sea freighters before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn space opera about people who are very good at being alone.

chapters.title: The Quiet Lane
chapters.summary: Vesper navigates the cargo hauler Long Answer through a deconflicted corridor, establishing their careful, invisible routine with engineer Doss and pilot Mireille. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine masking twelve years of deliberate self-erasure.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: A distress ping arrives encoded in Old Meridian, which Vesper recognizes from childhood lullabies no one else aboard knows. The crew debates ignoring it; Vesper lies and says it's static. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: first crack in the armor of invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Hold Remembers
chapters.summary: Vesper secretly plots the signal's origin while running cargo manifests as cover. Flashbacks reveal the accident that orphaned them and the backup program they fled. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: dread that the past has found a way to transmit.

chapters.title: Derelict at Verge Nine
chapters.summary: Against Mireille's objections, the crew docks with a drifting pre-Collapse freighter whose registry matches Vesper's family line. Its hold is cold but powered. POV: Mireille. Emotional beat: suspicion curdling into unease as Vesper's knowledge of the ship proves too intimate.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Sleepers
chapters.summary: Vesper opens the cryo bay alone: rows of pods, each holding a copy of themselves at different ages, including one labeled with their mother's name. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: horror and longing tangled together—the self multiplied into something unrecognizable.

chapters.title: The Syndicate's Interest
chapters.summary: A salvage syndicate corvette hails the Long Answer, claiming the derelict under an old writ and ordering the crew off. Their captain, Oyelaran, seems to know what's in the hold. POV: Mireille. Emotional beat: the crew realizes Vesper has dragged them into someone else's war.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Itemized
chapters.summary: Doss confronts Vesper over the lies; Mireille quietly reroutes the ship anyway, choosing her friend over safety. POV: Doss. Emotional beat: betrayal and forgiveness in the same breath—loyalty outlasting truth.

chapters.title: The Falsified Loop
chapters.summary: Deciphering the derelict's logs, Vesper learns the sleepers carry proof that Earth's famous final transmission was edited by the founding council to hide a deliberate abandonment. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: grief reframed as rage—the mourning of twelve years built on a manufactured message.

chapters.title: Wake One, Wake All
chapters.summary: Vesper begins reviving the oldest sleeper, a copy of themselves at nineteen, who wakes disoriented and hostile, insisting they are the original. POV: the awakened copy. Emotional beat: identity as argument—who gets to be real?

chapters.title: Oyelaran's Offer
chapters.summary: The syndicate captain boards under truce and offers Vesper amnesty in exchange for destroying the evidence and the sleepers. She reveals the council's descendants still rule the Verge. POV: Oyelaran. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: Mireille's Course
chapters.summary: Mireille lays in a run through contested orbit to reach a free relay station before the transmission loop decays past recovery. The crew votes; Doss abstains. POV: Mireille. Emotional beat: commitment—the moment hiding stops being an option for any of them.

chapters.title: Two of Me
chapters.summary: Vesper and the awakened copy argue through a long night watch about memory, guilt, and who owes whom a life. The copy reveals a memory Vesper has suppressed: their mother chose to stay behind. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: painful intimacy with oneself.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Shoals
chapters.summary: Syndicate hunters strike in a debris shoal; the Long Answer takes hull damage and Doss is injured shielding the drive. POV: Doss. Emotional beat: the cost of loyalty made physical.

chapters.title: The Loop Ends Tonight
chapters.summary: Calculations show Earth's transmission loop will decay below recoverable threshold within hours. Oyelaran offers a final ultimatum: surrender the sleepers or be hunted forever. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the clock becoming a character.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Vesper must decide: wake all two hundred copies (truth without enough resources to sustain them) or destroy the hold (safety built on the lie). The copy argues for waking; Mireille argues for survival. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the thematic fulcrum—identity versus continuity.

chapters.title: Relay Station Kettle
chapters.summary: The damaged ship limps into the free relay station, where stationmaster Iqbal offers a transmitter old enough to speak Old Meridian—if someone will claim authorship of the broadcast. POV: Iqbal. Emotional beat: witness; history requires a name attached.

chapters.title: The Council's Hand
chapters.summary: Council agents seize the station's docking ring; Oyelaran, revealed to be a descendant of the falsifiers' archivist, hesitates when shown the raw logs. POV: Oyelaran. Emotional beat: inherited guilt cracking open.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax: Vesper transmits the true final message in Old Meridian across the Verge while syndicate forces breach the station. The awakened copy holds the transmitter room, buying seconds with their life. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: truth spoken aloud at maximum cost.

chapters.title: One Pod Left
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, Vesper chooses: they wake only the sleeper bearing their mother's name and let the rest sleep on in trust, sealed and documented, until the Verge is ready. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: restraint as the hardest form of love.

chapters.title: Exile, Chosen
chapters.summary: The council brands Vesper a terrorist; the crew scatters to safe harbors. Vesper declines Mireille's offer of refuge, taking the Long Answer out alone. POV: Mireille. Emotional beat: farewell without bitterness—loyalty surviving separation.

chapters.title: Her Voice
chapters.summary: Far from the lanes, the mother-sleeper wakes. She remembers the real Earth, the real departure, and speaks Vesper's childhood name. POV: the mother. Emotional beat: recognition—the end of hiding.

chapters.title: An Echo for the Gravity
chapters.summary: Vesper and their mother chart a course toward the decaying loop itself, to keep its echo alive by repeating it, voice after voice, so the truth never falls silent again. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: resolution—not homecoming, but continuation; identity chosen rather than inherited.
